issuer: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
title: New Mexico TRD Ruling 495-13-1 Film Credit for Production Services and Expenditures
text:
Ruling 495-13-1
Issued: January 25, 2013
Effective: January 25, 2013
A ruling has been requested concerning the applicability of certain provisions of the Film
Production Tax Credit to the following facts:
X is a corporation which is a film production company as defined by Section 7-
2F-2(G), NMSA 1978. X will contract with Y, a company that will provide
goods and perform certain specialty services in New Mexico for the production of
the film. Y will neither be owned by X nor affiliated with X. Y will also provide
facilities, equipment (including but not limited to grip and electrical equipment,
camera equipment, props, set dressing, wardrobe, picture vehicles, hardware and
expendables), transportation and other material or activities to X. The equipment
will be purchased or leased by Y from various sources including manufacturers,
distributors, or other third-party merchandisers of equipment, who may be outside
the State of New Mexico. This may include employing or lending the services of
its employees to the production through a lending and assignment agreement. Y
will have physical presence at all times during the production in the state of New
Mexico from which the vendor conducts business, stores inventory or otherwise
creates, assembles or offers for sale or lease the product or services. Y will
employ laborers that include at least one New Mexico resident, but may have
employees that are not New Mexico residents. Individuals performing services for
Y under the contract between X and Y may not be residents of New Mexico.
X asks whether the amounts paid by X to Y will qualify for the film production tax credit if:
(1) X will pay Y directly under the Production Services Agreement (PSA) for goods and
services provided for the production of a film in New Mexico;
(2) Y is a New Mexico limited liability company and will at all times have physical
presence in the state of New Mexico during the production;
(3) X certifies that the services and other direct production expenditures for which the
credit is claimed were performed or provided by Y in New Mexico.
(4) X is eligible for the credit under Section 7-2F-1(K) NMSA 1978;
(5) X does not deliver to Y a nontaxable transaction certificate pursuant to Section 7-9-
86, NMSA 1978;
(6) Y will employ laborers that include at least one New Mexico resident, but may have
employees that are not New Mexico residents; and
(7) Y will purchase or lease equipment from various sources or other third-party
merchandisers of equipment, who may be outside of the State of New Mexico.
Relevant Law
Section 7-2F-1(A)(1) NMSA 1978 states in part that the film production tax credit is available to
an eligible film production company for “direct production expenditures made in New Mexico
that: (a) are directly attributable to the production in New Mexico of a film or commercial

audiovisual product; (b) are subject to taxation by the state of New Mexico; (c) exclude direct
production expenditures for which another taxpayer claims the film production tax credit; and (d)
do not exceed the usual and customary cost of the goods or services acquired when purchased by
unrelated parties.”
Section 7-2F-1(L) NMSA 1978 states:
L. The division shall determine the eligibility of the company and shall
report this information to the taxation and revenue department in a manner and at
times the economic development department and the taxation and revenue
department shall agree upon. The division shall also post on its web site all
information provided by the film production company that does not reveal
revenue, income or other information that may jeopardize the confidentiality of
income tax returns, including that the division shall report monthly the projected
amount of credit claims for the fiscal year.
Section 7-2F-2(C) NMSA 1978 states:
C. “direct production expenditure”:
(1) except as provided in Paragraph (2) of this subsection, means a
transaction that is subject to taxation in New Mexico, including:
(a) payment of wages, fringe benefits or fees for talent,
management or labor to a person who is a New Mexico resident;
(b) payment to a personal services business for the services
of a performing artist if the personal services business: 1) pays gross receipts tax
in New Mexico on the portion of those payments qualifying for the tax credit;
and; 2) deducts and remits withheld income tax pursuant to Subsection I of
Section 7-3A-3 NMSA 1978; and
(c) any of the following provided by a vendor: 1) the story and
scenario to be used for a film; 2) set construction and operations, wardrobe,
accessories and related services; 3) photography, sound synchronization, lighting
and related services; 4) editing and related services; 5) rental of facilities and
equipment; 6) leasing of vehicles, not including the chartering of aircraft for out-
of-state transportation; however, New Mexico-based chartered aircraft for in-state
transportation directly attributable to the production shall be considered a direct
production expenditure; provided that only the first one hundred dollars ($100) of
the daily expense of leasing a vehicle for passenger transportation on roadways in
the state may be claimed as a direct production expenditure; 7) food or lodging;
provided that only the first one hundred fifty dollars ($150) of lodging per
individual per day is eligible to be claimed as a direct production expenditure; 8)
commercial airfare if purchased through a New Mexico-based travel agency or
travel company for travel to and from New Mexico or within New Mexico that is
directly attributable to the production; 9) insurance coverage and bonding if
purchased through a New Mexico-based insurance agent, broker or bonding
agent; and 10) other direct costs of producing a film in accordance with generally
accepted entertainment industry practice; and

(2) does not include an expenditure for:
(a) a gift with a value greater than twenty-five dollars ($25.00);
(b) artwork or jewelry, except that a work of art or a piece of
jewelry may be a direct production expenditure if: 1) it is used in the film
production; and 2) the expenditure is less than two thousand five hundred dollars
($2,500); or
(c) entertainment, amusement or recreation;
Section 7-2F-2(M) NMSA 1978 states:
M. "vendor" means a person selling goods or services that has a physical
presence in New Mexico and is subject to gross receipts tax pursuant to the Gross
Receipts and Compensating Tax Act [7-9-1 NMSA 1978] and income tax
pursuant to the Income Tax Act [7-2-1 NMSA 1978] or corporate income tax
pursuant to the Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Act [7-2A-1 NMSA 1978].
Ruling
Provided that X is an eligible production company under the provisions of Section 7-2F-1(K)
NMSA 1978, X will be eligible for the credit in the amount equal to the percentage specified in
Section 7-2F-1(B) NMSA 1978 of the direct production expenditures that meet the requirements
of Sections 7-2F-1(A)(1) and 7-2F-2(C) NMSA1978. If Y meets the definition of vendor in
Section 7-2F-2(M) NMSA 1978, then Y is a vendor for purposes of the film production tax
credit. If the services provided by Y to X are listed in Section 7-2F-2(C)(1)(c) NMSA 1978,
subject to gross receipts tax in New Mexico, and Y employs laborers (some of which must be
New Mexico residents as defined in the Income Tax Act), then the expenditures for the services
are eligible for the film production tax credit.
If the facilities, equipment (including but not limited to grip and electrical equipment, camera
equipment, props, set dressing, wardrobe, picture vehicles, hardware and expendables),
transportation and other material and activities provided by Y to X are listed in and meet the
requirements of Section 7-2F-2(C)(1)(c) NMSA 1978, and are subject to taxation in New
Mexico, then the expenditures are eligible for the film production tax credit. If X is an eligible
production company, then on the Form RPD-41229, Application for Film Production Tax Credit,
X must certify the qualifying direct production expenditures reported on the claim:
• include only expenditures made in New Mexico directly attributable to the approved
production;
• include only transactions which are subject to taxation by the State of New Mexico;
• exclude expenditures for which another taxpayer claims the film production tax
credit; and
• exclude expenditures for which the film production company delivered a nontaxable
transaction certificate pursuant to Section 7-9-86 NMSA 1978.
However, certification by X is not sufficient by itself. The New Mexico Film Division of the
Economic Development Department must determine eligibility of the company, pursuant to
Section 7-2F-1(L) NMSA 1978, and report this information to the Taxation and Revenue

Department. Moreover, as with all film credit applications, the Taxation and Revenue
Department will review invoices from Y to X and other documentation to determine whether
claimed expenditures meet statutory and regulatory requirements.
